subject: Ephemeral quota amendment & provisional true-up — Cobalt Retail
messages:
From: Natalie Owens <natalie@cobaltretail.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary quota bump for Sep 10-14 campaign

Hi Markus,

Hope you’re well — quick ask from our side. We have a planned marketing push (paid social + email) scheduled Sep 10–14 that will spike our inference usage for product recommendations and on-site search. Based on internal projections the peak will be ~2M additional tokens/day across the four-day window (roughly a 300% uplift vs our current committed throughput).

We need to understand options for a short-term quota increase (ephemeral headroom) and how Redwood would handle billing for overrun/true-up. Specifically:
- Can we get a provisional quota increase for Sep 10–14 (expected start 00:00 09/10 PT)?
- What blended overrun rate would you apply for that window (vs. our committed rate)?
- Any launch/one-time credits available if we sign PO for the temporary uplift now?
- Can you confirm behavior when we hit per-minute rate limits — is there graceful throttling or hard rejects?

Procurement needs a line-item estimate for PO creation by EOD 2026-09-06. I attached a short summary of projected usage (Cobalt_TrueUp_Summary.pdf).

If helpful, Tom Hayes (cc) is our engineering lead and can share traffic patterns. We appreciate any quick guidance — this is time-sensitive.

Thanks,
Natalie Owens
Head of Product Operations
Cobalt Retail

Attachments: Cobalt_TrueUp_Summary.pdf (1 page)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Owens <natalie@cobaltretail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quota bump for Sep 10-14 campaign

Hi Natalie — thanks for the details and the summary. I looped in Ben (sales ops) and Laura (finance) to align on billing mechanics and procurement needs. Quick read below and a provisional path we can execute if you can approve the PO by 2026-09-06.

Proposal (short window, Sep 10–14):
- Provisional ephemeral quota: 3x your current committed QPS for the 00:00–23:59 PT window each day (safety cap per minute to avoid noisy failures).
- Billing: Overrun true-up at a blended rate: committed rate + 30% premium for the first 72 hours of uplift, reverting to committed + 10% thereafter for the remainder of the window.
- Launch credit: one-time $5,000 launch credit applied to the first invoice if PO received by 2026-09-06 and the uplift is accepted as a provisional amendment.
- Throttling behavior: graceful shedding with token-prioritization — we prefer throttling over hard rejects; we’ll configure fallback to your lower-cost model variant if we detect persistent queueing.
- Procurement deliverables: Ben will attach an itemized estimate (line items: provisional quota days, additional token estimate, applied launch credit, estimated invoice date).

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the provisional terms (or highlight any line items you want adjusted). If accepted, we’ll send a short amendment/PO template and Ben will add the spreadsheet with exact cost rows.

cc: Tom Hayes for technical confirmation.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com | +1 (510) 555-0198

Attachments: Provisional_Quota_Amendment_20260903.xlsx (placeholder — final numbers pending)
From: Natalie Owens <natalie@cobaltretail.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-03T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quota bump for Sep 10-14 campaign

Markus — appreciate the quick reply. A few clarifications so procurement can finalize the PO: 

1) Blended rate: committed +30% for first 72 hours is higher than we were expecting. Can you show a worked example for ~2M extra tokens/day (line item estimate) and a secondary option at committed +15% if we accept a slightly lower launch credit?

2) Throttling & fallbacks: we need a firm SLA on request semantics — if you will gracefully shed, can you confirm error rates we might see at peak and fallback latency to the cheaper variant? Our engineering lead Tom is okay with the fallback but needs the expected 95th percentile latency for the fallback model.

3) Invoice timing: we need the overrun charge to fall on the October invoice (we have strict month-end budgeting). Can Redwood delay billing for this true-up until Oct if we sign the PO by 9/06?

Procurement will not sign a PO without an itemized cost table. If you can provide both options (Option A: committed+30% with $5k credit; Option B: committed+15% with $2k credit), that would be ideal.

I’m attaching an updated projection chart from Tom in case that helps (embedded in Cobalt_TrueUp_Summary.pdf). Can Ben/Laura respond with the two options and the sample estimate?

Thanks,
Natalie

On Sep 2, 2026, at 3:10 PM, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> (previous message quoted)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Owens <natalie@cobaltretail.com>

Date: 2026-09-04T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quota bump for Sep 10-14 campaign — cost options

Hi Natalie / Tom — Ben here. Thanks for the clear asks. Below are two explicit options with worked numbers (rounded) based on your 2M extra tokens/day estimate. Assumptions: current committed unit price = $0.0008 per token, projected uplift = 2M tokens/day x 4 days = 8M tokens additional.

Option A (faster approval, larger credit):
- Rate: committed + 30% => $0.00104 per token
- Gross uplift cost: 8,000,000 * $0.00104 = $8,320
- Launch credit: $5,000 (applied to first invoice)
- Net uplift charge: $3,320
- Billing timing: we can defer the overrun invoice to October as requested if PO received by 2026-09-06.

Option B (smaller credit, lower premium):
- Rate: committed + 15% => $0.00092 per token
- Gross uplift cost: 8,000,000 * $0.00092 = $7,360
- Launch credit: $2,000
- Net uplift charge: $5,360
- Billing timing: same deferral to October possible with PO by 9/06, but the credit and lower premium require us to mark the uplift as prepaid on the PO (simple line item).

Operational notes:
- Throttling: default is graceful shedding; we estimate <1.5% error rate at 95th percentile during the uplift with the fallback model. Fallback latency for the cheaper variant: 95th percentile ~420ms per request under the projected load (we’ll validate with a pre-launch run if you want).
- PO deliverable: we’ll provide an itemized spreadsheet with line items (I’ve attached the provisional sheet) and a short amendment template.

If you approve either option, we’ll generate the amendment and apply the launch credit conditionally on timely PO. Happy to hop on a 15-minute call if you want to run the numbers live.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
